title: Horse-Drawn Carriage Making
text: “Oink.”
When we arrived at the magic shop, an old pig looked at my Father and me with a puzzled expression. Though his gaze quickly softened.
“Oink-oink.”
“Um… when you check for magical aptitude, do you look at which type of magic someone is good at?”
“Oink.”
“Apparently, my Father has an aptitude for healing and support magic.”
There’s no need to have him checked. I’d already heard about my Father’s aptitude from the future. My Father from the future had mastered some truly excellent support Magic.
“Oink-oink? Oink-oink-oink?”
“We don’t really have much money to pay for a reading…”
That’s the problem, isn’t it? We’ve made all sorts of preparations for our traveling trade, but when it comes to money, our finances are pretty tight right now.
“Oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink?”
“Magic orbs? What are those?”

I remember this well. After my Father—who’d been framed and threw money at me—left, Trash gave the remaining heroes magic orbs as a special reward that allowed them to learn spells. They were great for beginners. Plus, he’d give us more whenever we asked, so the situation was really favorable.

However, when you learn magic from an orb, the power is lower than when you learn it from Magic Books. You can’t make fine adjustments either, and if I’d relied solely on that method, I’m certain I wouldn’t have been able to master Liberation-class magic.
“Big talk?”
“The distribution of those orbs that let you learn magic easily happens after my Father leaves.”
“I-I see… Just how far do they plan to discriminate…”
“Well, if you have the money to spare, you can always buy a Magic Book.”
“Booh.”

It seems Keel is staring at the crystal in the back of the magic shop. Sakura-chan is standing still, as if following Father’s lead. She’s very well-behaved, unlike the Sakura-chan I used to know. Well, Sakura-chan is naturally a gentle-natured child, after all.
“Boo.”

The magic shop owner beckons us toward the back of the store. Then, he starts rummaging around back there. After a while, a familiar piece of equipment appears. It looks like a spinning wheel—indeed, that device converts Magical Power into thread.
“Motoyasu-kun. How much does that cost?”
“Boo-boo-boo-boo-boo-hee”
“Oh, is the old man throwing that in for free? That’s a big help.”
It seems… he’s taking the weapons I gave him in trade. Looks like the old man at the weapon shop has been laying the groundwork for this.
“Thank you very much.”
“While we’re at it, could you give me a Magic Book as well?”
“Boo-hee”
“Motoyasu-kun. Honestly, I’d like you to save up and buy that one yourself.”
I suppose there’s no helping it. I’d love for my father to learn Magic, but it’s quite difficult to master. Maybe he can take his time learning it later?
“Oink.”
“Oh, okay. Just wait a sec.”

Sakura-chan stepped forward, took off her clothes in the corner of the room, and transformed into the Filolial Queen. Before she transformed, my father was considerate enough to turn his back. Ah, what a shame. Her color scheme is the exact opposite of Filo-tan’s. The magic shopkeeper seems surprised.

Sakura spins the spindle slowly in a circle, spinning her thread. She’s so laid-back that, just like last time, she’s moving at a snail’s pace, and everyone’s starting to get bored. Fortunately, at least no one’s falling asleep like last time.
“Sakura’s taking way too long.”
“Now, now, everyone works at their own pace, so Yuki-chan, please be patient.”
“But…”
“That’s right. If you have some free time, could you ask Motoyasu-kun to help get a carriage? I think Sakura-chan will be done by then.”
“Come to think of it, it’s about time.”
It’s not that I’d forgotten. It’s just that getting a carriage is a hassle in its own right. If we’re looking for a carriage that isn’t too flashy, it’d be faster to build one ourselves.

Or, raiding a band of bandits who own a carriage and taking it from them would be the quickest solution… But as a stopgap measure, maybe we should just buy a handcart? Those are pretty cheap, and if we get some wood and convert it into a carriage, we should be able to make it work. Yeah.
“Well then, I’ll go get a carriage.”
“Leave it to you.”
“Yes, sir. What size should we go for?”
“We’ve got quite a few people, so I think a slightly larger one would be good.”
“Understood. Alright, Yuki-chan, Kou! Let’s go!”
“Understood.”
“Okay!”

Yuki-chan, Kou, and I left the magic shop to procure a cart. We headed for the mountains near Riyute Village. We’ll cut down some trees with our spears. With my Attack Power, cutting down trees is as easy as slicing tofu, so we’ll chop them down and build a cart. Filolial-sama absolutely love pulling carriages. Believe it or not, I’ve actually built not just carts, but carriages as well.

The slightly troublesome part is making the wheels. Let’s make it a completely wooden cart for now and see how long it lasts. If necessary, I’ll have my dad build the metal carriage that Filo-tan used to love.

To be honest, the reason I hold the weapons shop owner in such high regard is that he built Filo-tan’s carriage. I know he’s quite skilled. I did think, “A weapons shop making carriages…?” but Filo-tan was so proud of it.
“Kitamura, let’s adjust the wheel size.”
“Kou. You’ll need to file it down a bit more or it won’t sit right.”
“Got it.”
“You need to bring out the sheen.”
Yuki-chan and Kou are hard at work building the cart. And just like polishing with feathers, they’re carefully shaping the wood to bring out that sheen.
“It’s best to lightly char it.”

I adjusted my Magic to shape the wood, carved out the wheel hubs, and assembled them. Since we’ll be crossing mountain passes, it needs to be at least minimally functional. Of course, I made sure it could turn left and right. And just like that, the cart was finished; all that’s left is to attach the canopy and turn it into a horse-drawn carriage.
“We did it!”
“The joy is twice as great when we all work together, isn’t it?”
“It’s complete!”
A magnificent carriage, sparkling in my eyes, had been created. Just then, I looked up at the sky and saw that the sun was beginning to set. It had taken longer than I expected.
“Well then, let’s head back to Father.”
“Okay!”
“I’ll pull it.”
“Kou’s gonna pull it!”
Yuki-chan and the others started fighting over who would hold the carriage’s handle.
“We’ll take turns. Yuki-chan goes first. When we’re about halfway to the town, Kou can take over.”
“Got it.”
“Got it!”
We hopped into the carriage and set off to see Father.
My father and the others were waiting in front of the Magic shop in town.
“W-welcome back… That’s a brand-new carriage. It must’ve cost a pretty penny, didn’t it?”
“I built it myself.”
“W-wow. Motoyasu, you can build carriages?”
“I can easily cut through wood with my spear, after all.”
“Huh…”
My father is running his hand over the carriage I built to check it out.
“Well, let’s get going then.”
“Oof!”
Keel is looking at the carriage with great interest. Sakura-chan looks sleepy. Though she usually does look sleepy, anyway.
“Ah, Motoyasu-kun. I had the thread made from Magical Power turned into fabric, but what should we do with it now? I could’ve taken it to a Tailor, though.”
“I’ll make it myself. Sakura-chan”
“Hmm? Well… something like what Yuki-chan is wearing? No way—”
“What do you mean by that!?”
Yuki-chan reacted to Sakura-chan’s request. With Yuki-chan’s anger blown away by the wind, Sakura-chan turns her gaze toward her Father.
“Does Sakura-chan dislike dresses?”
“Hmm… I don’t hate them, but they’re just not my style.”
“Then would you prefer something like Kou’s?”
Kou is wearing overalls. It gives off a mischievous vibe—very nice.
“That’s not quite right either.”
“Then would you prefer regular clothes?”
Pointing at the outfits of the townspeople passing by, I ask.
“Something like that.”
Hmm… It sounds like the kind of clothes Big Sister used to wear under her armor. Let’s picture that.
“Got it. Now, Father and everyone, please get into the carriage.”
“Ah, yeah. All that’s left is to go get the commercial pass that the envoy from Siltvelt prepared for us.”
“That’s right. So, shall we go pick it up as promised?”
“Yeah. Let’s get in then.”
Following Father’s instructions, Sakura-chan and Keel got into the carriage.
“Well then, let’s get going!”

At the sound of my voice, Kou, who was driving the carriage, set off cheerfully. With a clatter, the carriage left the castle town and continued on its way before the sun set. Is it even worth mentioning that, in less than an hour, Keel had fallen down from motion sickness?
